Uṣasti Cākrāyaṇa
------------------------------------------
Uṣasti Cākrāyaṇa was an young ब्राह्मण priest who lived in the Ibhya-grāma (a village inhabited by mahouts). Once the crops of that area were destroyed by hailstorms resulting in a severe famine. Uṣasti secured a few forest beans that were being eaten by a mahout and then managed to go to the place where a king was performing a sacrifice. Seeing that the priests like the prastotā, the udgātā as also the pratihartā (the priests representing the Sāmaveda) were ignorant of the deities connected with the mantras they were to chant, he challenged them to reveal the same. When they fell silent, the king enquired who he was. Coming to know his identity, the king was happy since he had been searching for him, without success, to assist in his sacrifice. At the request of the king, उषस्ति चाक्रायण accepted the responsibility of completing the sacrifice.
Later on, at the specific requests of the three priests he taught them the three deities: प्राण for प्रस्ताव; आदित्य for उद्गीथ and अन्न for प्रतिहार.
Prastāva, उद्गीथ and प्रतिहार are the first three of the five fundamental steps in the singing of a sāma chant.
The whole episode appears in the Chāndogya Upaniṣad (1.10; 1.11).

Uṣā
------------------------------------------
She was the daughter of Bāṇāsura, a demon king who was a contemporary of Śrī कृष्ण. Once she dreamt of अनिरुद्ध —grandson of Śrī Kṛṣṇa—and fell in love with him. Citralekhā, her servant-maid who had magical powers, transported अनिरुद्ध surreptitiously to Uṣā’s place. The couple lived happily for some time. However, when Bāṇāsura came to know of it, he imprisoned both of them. Later on, Śrī कृष्ण invaded Bāṇāsura’s capital, defeated him and freed both of them (vide Bhāgavata 10.62 and 63).

Uṣas
(‘one who shines’)
------------------------------------------
In the Ṛgveda dawn has been deified as the goddess उषस्. There are twenty sūktas devoted to her.
These sūktas are highly poetical descriptions of the goddess.
A few of these may be given here as a sample:
She is eternal since she comes every-day, in the same form (1.92.10).
She destroys darkness that has enveloped the world (1.92.4).
She wakes up all beings and engages them in their work (4.51.5).
She comes in a brilliant golden chariot (1.48.7).
Sūrya, the Sun, is her husband (7.75.5).
Only after her arrival, fires begin to burn and sacrifices are undertaken (7.80.1).
The Vedic sage prays to her to give him wealth and long life (7.82.6).

Uśanas
------------------------------------------
Uśanas is an ancient sage mentioned even in the Ṛgveda (8.84; 9.87, 88, 89). There, his name is stated as काव्य उशनस्. He helped इन्द्र to get back the cows abducted by the Paṇis (a tribe with a bad reputation).
Lord कृष्ण says in the Bhagavadgītā (10.37) that he is उशनस् among the kavis or wise men.
Since कौटिल्य (300 B. C.) has quoted उशनस् several times, it can be surmised that he was the author of an important treatise on political science.
The Pañcaviṁśa Brāhmaṇa (7.5.20) states that उशनस् was the priest of the असुरस्. He is thus identified with शुक्राचार्य, the गुरु of the असुरस्, as depicted in the epics and the पुराणस्.
Two works attributed to him are available in the manuscript form.
They are: Auśanasa-dharmaśāstra and Auśanasa-dharmasūtra.
The Auśanasa-dharmaśāstra is in prose with a few verses. A few of the more important subjects dealt with are: अशौच (ceremonial impurity on birth and death); the four varṇas and mixed castes; prāyaścittas or expiations; śrāddha (obsequial rites); punishment for महापातकस् (heinous sins); fourteen kinds of sciences (known as Caturdaśa-विद्यास्).
The Auśanasa-dharmasūtra contains several passages in prose. Several divergent views of वसिष्ठ, हारीत, शौनक and गौतम are quoted on some important points.
From the quotations in other works it is reasonable to conclude that there was a work by उशनस् dealing with the subjects like आचार (daily conduct), vyavahāra (secular and social dealings) and प्रायश्चित्त.
Another work called Auśanasa-smṛti has also been discovered. It contains 600 verses spread over nine chapters. It deals with the following subjects: उपनयन, Vedic studies, dharmas of a स्नातक (See SNĀTAKA for details.), śrāddha and prāyaścittas (expiations for sins).
Uśanas has been quoted by several dharmaśāstra writers.
The Śukranītisāra of शुक्राचार्य is definitely a late work and has nothing to do with उशनस्.
